title: How to text from a different number: 7 best apps
summary: Want a separate number to text your customers? Learn how to text from a different number and find out the seven apps you should use.
body_markdown:
Your small business is finally taking off, but your cell phone is buzzing non-stop. You try to answer every call, but you’re still overloaded with customer texts and personal messages in your inbox. How do you separate business communications from your personal life without carrying two phones or missing important calls?


What you need is a second phone number. When you text customers from a different number, you can automatically separate your conversations and protect your peace of mind.


There are four ways to text customers with a different number:


- **A business texting app** takes a few minutes to set up and gives you access to shared local and toll-free numbers to text customers. You can also use business-friendly texting features like scheduled texts, text templates, and automated text workflows to automatically send messages as needed. .
- **A free texting app** also gives you access to local phone numbers. However, you won’t be able to share them with your team. They also don’t come with any advanced texting features. .
- **A carrier second line** gives you a different number directly from your mobile provider. Add-ons like Verizon Second Number add another number to your existing plan. They operate just like a personal phone number, so you can’t share them with your team. You’ll need a phone with dual SIM or eSIM features to use this method.


Want the flexibility of phone numbers from multiple carriers? You can get your own **second SIM or eSIM.** This works just like a carrier second line, but you[get a second phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-second-phone-number/) from a different carrier.


Keep in mind that if you’re texting customers on behalf of your company, business texting rules apply. You’ll need to file for carrier registration, also known as[A2P 10DLC](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a2p-10dlc/) registration, for your business number. You also need to collect[SMS consent](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-consent/) from customers before messaging them.


##


4 Ways to text from a different number


Here are four options to consider if you want to send texts from a different number:

### 1. Get a virtual phone number with a VoIP service

For example, you may have to upgrade or contact support just to add new users or numbers. And choosing a provider without the right features might leave you without the tools you need, like[VoIP integrations](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-integrations/) ,[shared inboxes](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/) , or[automated responses](https://www.quo.com/blog/text-message-autoresponder/) .

You can also bring your existing number into Quo with[phone number porting](https://www.quo.com/blog/whats-phone-number-porting/) .
3. **Verify your account.** Confirm your account with an existing cell phone number and a credit card.
4. **Register to text in the US.** Once you’ve activated your account and completed your free trial, you can[complete US carrier registration](https://support.quo.com/getting-started/carrier-registration/carrier-registration#all-openphone-users-must-register-to-text-us-numbers) to text US phone numbers. This additional step is a requirement for any virtual phone number due to emerging regulations pushed by the large US cell carriers.


That’s it! You now have a virtual phone number ready to use on your iPhone, Android, laptop, or tablet. You can add your team members to a shared number, set up integrations, access call recordings and transcripts, and more.

### 2. Use a free texting app


One of the easiest ways to text from a different number is by using a free texting app like TextNow or TextFree. While you do get a free number to text your contacts, their ads can be intrusive. Some providers also reclaim your number due to inactivity. For example, TextFree numbers expire if you don’t send a text for 30 days. You won’t get features for[call management](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management) , either.


Another option is to use an app geared towards mass SMS marketing, like SimpleTexting. Plans start at $39.99 per month and include 500 text credits per month and a local number. You can use this number to send and receive SMS/MMS messages separately from your personal line.


While the initial cost may seem low, additional fees for premium features or additional texting credits can add up. And if you have a team, these apps might not support multiple users or shared numbers, making it hard for your business to scale.


### 3. Get a second number with your existing cell carrier


Many major cell carriers like AT&T,[Verizon](https://www.quo.com/blog/verizon-second-number-alternatives/) , and[T-Mobile](https://www.quo.com/blog/t-mobile-business-alternatives/) offer services that let you add a second phone number to your device. Visit your provider’s website and check what services they offer for setting up additional numbers. You can also contact their customer support and ask if it’s possible to text from a different number on your current plan. Make sure to ask about the costs and requirements.


All these second number plans require a dual- SIM or eSIM-enabled phone. While your provider might assign you a second number, you’ll need an eSIM or a physical SIM card to activate it. Here’s the thing: not all smartphones support dual SIM cards, so you might need to invest in a new device. You’ll also rack up extra costs for the second SIM card and a separate mobile plan. You also won’t get business-friendly features that’ll help your team grow. These numbers operate just like your personal number.


### **4. Get a separate SIM card**


Your fourth option is to get a second SIM card for your **unlocked** phone. This gives you a separate number for texting and calling, effectively splitting your personal and professional chats.


This option is similar to getting a second phone number from your existing carrier. The difference is you can get a second SIM card from another carrier to maximize your network access. Similar to the previous option, this requires a phone with dual SIM or eSIM capabilities. It also doesn’t offer business-friendly features like shared numbers, CRM integrations, or AI call summaries.

##


6 powerful reasons to text from a different number


**


Texting from a different number isn’t just about separating work from personal life. Here are six more reasons it’s a smart move for you and your business:


### **1. Scale easily as your team grows**


Add more lines as your team expands or segment numbers by location, department, or project. Local and toll-free numbers, for instance, help you serve different markets.


### **2. Share responsibility with your team**


Use[shared lines](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management/shared-line-appearance) and call forwarding to distribute workload so no client communication falls through the cracks. With Quo’s shared inbox, your whole team has visibility into customer conversations.


### **3. Improve work-life balance**


Set business hours to make sure you aren’t disturbed during your personal time. This helps prevent burnout for you and your team. Set up routing options and auto-replies for after-hours so your customers aren’t left waiting.


### **4. Organize client communications**


Keep all your communications in one place and maintain a clear record of calls, texts, voicemails, and interactions for better context and accountability. If a dispute arises with a customer or employee, you’ll have documentation ready.


### **5. Integrate with existing tools**


Connect your virtual phone number app with CRM systems, email marketing tools, and more to automate workflows and save time. This reduces manual data entry that drains productivity and let details slip through the cracks.


### **6. Protect your business from spam calls**


Spam calls waste time and are tricky to detect. A second number on a virtual phone app can prevent spam from reaching you. Most apps let you set up an auto-attendant, which robocalls can’t navigate. The result is more time for your team to focus on the customer experience.


##


Is your data safe in a second number app?


As you evaluate options for a second phone number, you might wonder whether your data is secure in a virtual phone platform.


Business phone platforms like Quo encrypt your texts and calls, so conversations stay private between you and your customers. Independent auditors regularly review these security practices through SOC 2 audits. For healthcare businesses, some providers offer a HIPAA-compliant platform to manage patient communications. Since business phone providers make their money from customer subscriptions, not from selling data, your information isn’t a product; it’s yours to export or take with you whenever you need to.


With free second number apps like TextFree and TextNow, you aren’t guaranteed these protections. They make money from selling ads, and they don’t advertise data encryption or compliance standards. Keep that in mind as you evaluate which path to choose for your second phone number.


##


Business texting requirements: What you should know


Once you get a second phone number, you can dial your customers and call from a different number. However, you can’t start texting them immediately. You have to follow the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, or[TCPA](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/11/06/2024-24908/rules-and-regulations-implementing-the-telephone-consumer-protection-act-of-1991) , and the Cellular Telecommunications and Internet Association, or[CTIA](https://api.ctia.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/230523-CTIA-Messaging-Principles-and-Best-Practices-FINAL.pdf) , regulations. Here’s what you need to do to stay compliant:


### 1. Get SMS opt-in


You must obtain customer consent to send text messages. You aren’t allowed to message their phone number unless you get their consent first. If a customer texts you first using an SMS link or WhatsApp, you have implied consent, but that only applies to the conversation at hand. Otherwise, customers need to[opt in](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-does-opt-mean-in-text/) via a digital or physical form, which you should keep in your records.


### 2. Register your second phone number


When you have a second phone number from a business phone app, you need to register it under[A2P 10DLC](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a2p-10dlc/) compliance regulations. A2P 10DLC stands for Application-to-Person 10-Digit Long Code. This means that if you use a virtual number to text anyone with a US phone number on behalf of your business, you need to complete US carrier registration. The A2P 10DLC process varies by provider.


Once your number is registered, you can start texting customers in the US. But compliance doesn’t end there.


### **3. Follow compliance rules when texting customers**


Stay informed about regulations and follow[SMS consent](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-consent/) rules. Under[TCPA compliance guidelines](https://www.quo.com/blog/tcpa-compliance-checklist/) , companies can’t send promotional texts or call individuals outside 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. These times are based on your recipient’s time zone. It’s also good[texting etiquette](https://www.quo.com/blog/business-texting-etiquette-tips/) to send non-urgent messages during regular business hours.


You should also give your customers an easy way to unsubscribe from your texts. For example, you should tell them they can say something like: “Reply END to stop receiving texts.”


These are the basic business texting requirements you should follow. For a full breakdown on everything you need to know, check out our guide to[SMS compliance](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-compliance/) .


##


**Business texting vs personal texting: Key differences**


When you’re texting for business, you need to do more than just send messages. Business texting providers offer features personal texting apps don’t. These enable customer communication, team collaboration, and professional compliance:


- **Unlimited texts and calls.** Send as many messages as you need without worrying about hitting limits during busy periods.
- **Shared numbers.** Multiple team members can call and text from the same number so customers get a response — even when you’re unavailable.
- **Automations like auto-replies and scheduled texts.** Keep customers in the loop without being glued to your phone 24/7 through automated responses and pre-scheduled messages.
- **Text forwarding.** Route incoming messages to the right team members to make sure customers get a quick response.
- **Customer history and context.** Use contact notes and CRM integrations to access conversation history. This shows customer details at a glance so you can provide personalized responses every time.

FAQs


**Can I hide my number for a single text without an app?**


Carrier codes such as *67 mask your phone number when you make calls. This doesn’t apply to texts. If you want to hide your personal number while texting a contact, your best bet is to get a second phone number specifically for business texting.


**Can I send MMS and group texts from a second number?**


Business phone providers like Quo offer MMS and group texting features in their platforms. Free apps like Burner may have these features with limitations. For example, Burner offers both features, but only for iOS users. Android users won’t find these features in their Burner app.


**How can I text from a different number for free?**

**How can I forward a text message to another phone number?**

**How does texting from a different number using VoIP technology work?**


Voice over Internet Protocol technology allows you to send texts and make calls over the internet instead of traditional phone lines. This means you can get[texts on your computer](https://www.quo.com/blog/send-text-from-computer/) , tablet, or smartphone and send messages without needing a separate physical phone line.


**Should I use text forwarding or get a virtual phone number for my business?**


A virtual phone number makes more sense than text forwarding for businesses. Forwarding just pushes messages from one device to another and doesn’t give your team a way to work together.


VoIP systems keep all your texts, calls, and voicemails with a customer in one shared thread so your whole team can stay on the same page.
